title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is from the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes. A (pre)atelier (M, <=, <<) is compared with the model of 'figures' Fig(L) in a set L of points.
- Each figure has a shadow omb(X), a subset of L.
- X <= Y means 'sub-figure'.
- X << Y is a stronger 'significant/essential containment'. On p.59, for a point x, x << X means x lies in omb(X).
- A further relation (written with a crossed asymptotic sign) expresses compatibility of two figures.
A realization map phi sends abstract figures to figures in L, with |phi(F)| = omb(F). Page 57 states the corollary in its corrected form: (i) [phi is an 'ensembliste' embedding] implies (ii) plus injectivity of phi, and Grothendieck sets out to prove the converse, (ii) + phi injective => (i). He splits this into a), b), c); a) is already done.

Proof of c). Assume phi is injective and let H be the common sub-figure of F and G. Then phi(H) is the largest common sub-figure of phi(F) and phi(G). Compatibility of phi(F) and phi(G) means |phi(F)| ∩ |phi(G)| = |phi(H)|, i.e. omb(F) ∩ omb(G) = omb(H). By an axiom of the atelier (referred to as 'Ab CL (ope)'?), this is exactly the criterion for F and G to be compatible. So c) holds.

Attempt at b). Show that phi(F) << phi(G) implies F << G. Using a), he reduces to generators X, Y in M, and then exclaims: 'Mais c'est ... faux!'

Counterexample. Take Figpol(L), the polyhedral figures in L (with polyhedral triangulations), with <= as usual and << taken as the polyhedral relation <<_pol. The bare set-theoretic relation <<_ens (inclusion of shadows) is weaker. He notes in passing that replacing <<_ens by <<_pol does not affect the validity of the axioms Prat 1'–Prat 6'. Now take two strict polyhedral figures X, Y, e.g. simplices Δ1, Δ2, with X <<_ens Y but not X <<_pol Y. Their images satisfy the set-level relation, but the abstract relation fails.

Consequence. 'Ensembliste' must be relativized. On p.59 this leads to separate notions: 'ensembliste spécial' vs 'ensembliste polyédral', and 'quasi-ensembliste' (condition (ii) only), with axioms Prat quasi 1–4.

Purpose. Axiomatizing a 'tame' (moderate) topology in which figures are combinatorial/polyhedral objects together with their point-set shadows, and characterizing when an abstract atelier is faithfully represented by sets.
errors: The originally intended corollary ((ii) + injectivity of phi ⇒ (i)) is false, as Grothendieck himself discovers on this page via the polyhedral counterexample. The proof of c) is fine modulo the unstated axiom 'Ab CL (ope)'.
The counterexample is only sketched. He never specifies concretely two simplices with <<_ens but not <<_pol, nor exactly what <<_pol means.

ideas.what: Faithful set-theoretic realization of an abstract structure of 'figures' with sub-figure, essential-containment and compatibility relations, determined by shadows (supports) in a point set
ideas.modern_name: axiomatics of tame topology / representation of a combinatorial 'site' of figures by subsets (cf. o-minimal structures, PL topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: tame topology program: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984) as motivation; realized by van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (o-minimality)
ideas.where_published: Only the general call for 'topologie modérée' appears in Esquisse d'un programme §5; the atelier axiomatics are unpublished.

ideas.what: Counterexample: set-theoretic inclusion of supports (<<_ens) is strictly weaker than polyhedral essential containment (<<_pol), so injectivity plus the quasi-set-theoretic condition does not give a faithful embedding
ideas.modern_name: distinction between set-theoretic and structured (PL) subobject relations

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 'atelier/préatelier' axiomatics for analysis situs (figures, shadows, relations <=, <<, compatibility, axioms Prat 1'–6') is an unpublished abstract framework for tame topology, distinct from o-minimality. On this page he finds that faithfulness needs to be relativized (ensembliste vs polyédral).
missed.quote: Mais c'est ... faux! ... Considérons deux figures strictes polyédrales ... avec X <<_ens Y et non X <<_pol Y, on a le contre-exemple.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor technical step within a larger unexplored axiomatization of tame topology that could be compared with o-minimal and 'tame' structures. Taken alone, the page is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine verification and self-correction inside the unpublished atelier axiomatics. The framework as a whole is little known, but this page holds no notable standalone result.
transcription_corrections: 'ombr(F) ∩ ombr(G) = ombr(H)' should read 'omb(F) ∩ omb(G) = omb(H)'.
'Utilisant ces déf. prouvé' is likely 'Utilisant a) déjà prouvé, on est ramené au cas X, Y ∈ M'.
'Mais c'est un [?] faux!' is likely 'Mais c'est encore faux!'.
The interlinear addition above 'polyédrales dans L' looks like '(+ triangulations polyédrales)', not 'ombrées polyédrales'.
In the last line the first relation is X <<_ens Y ('ens' written under <<), contrasted with non X <<_pol Y.
